text: Paris is the capital and most populous city of France, located along the Seine river in the north of the country.
Mount Everest, located in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and Tibet, is the highest mountain above sea level on Earth.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen.
The theory of relativity, developed by Albert Einstein, describes how space and time are linked for objects moving at a consistent speed in a straight line.
A neural network is a computing system inspired by biological brains, made up of layers of interconnected nodes that learn patterns from data.
Cloud computing allows users to access computing resources such as servers, storage, and databases over the internet rather than owning physical hardware.
The printing press, invented by Johannes Gutenberg in the 15th century, revolutionized the spread of information across Europe.
The Silk Road was a network of trade routes connecting the East and West, facilitating the exchange of goods, ideas, and culture for centuries.
Sourdough bread gets its distinctive tangy flavor from a fermented starter made of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria.
Sushi is a traditional Japanese dish that typically combines vinegared rice with seafood, vegetables, and sometimes tropical fruits.
The Amazon rainforest, spanning several South American countries, is the largest tropical rainforest in the world and a critical regulator of global oxygen and carbon cycles.
The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert on Earth, stretching across much of North Africa and covering an area comparable to the size of the United States.
DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is a molecule that carries the genetic instructions used in the growth, development, and reproduction of all known living organisms.
The periodic table organizes chemical elements by increasing atomic number, revealing recurring patterns in their physical and chemical properties.
Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that records transactions across multiple computers so that records cannot be altered retroactively without altering all subsequent blocks.
Quantum computing uses principles of quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement, to process information in ways that classical computers cannot.
The Roman Empire, at its height, spanned three continents and left a lasting legacy on law, architecture, and language throughout Europe and beyond.
The Industrial Revolution, beginning in the late 18th century, transformed manufacturing processes and reshaped economies through mechanization and factory production.
Kimchi is a traditional Korean side dish made from salted and fermented vegetables, most commonly napa cabbage and Korean radish, seasoned with chili pepper and garlic.
Olive oil, a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, is produced by pressing whole olives and is prized for its flavor and health benefits, particularly its monounsaturated fats.
The Great Barrier Reef, off the coast of Queensland, Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system, visible even from outer space.
Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest and oldest freshwater lake in the world, holding about a fifth of the planet's unfrozen surface fresh water.
The Nile River, flowing through northeastern Africa, is traditionally considered the longest river in the world and was central to the rise of ancient Egyptian civilization.
Black holes are regions of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape once it crosses the event horizon.
Vaccines work by training the immune system to recognize and fight specific pathogens, often using a weakened, inactivated, or partial form of the disease-causing agent.
Plate tectonics describes how the Earth's outer shell is divided into several plates that glide over the mantle, driving earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain formation.
The Internet of Things refers to the network of physical devices embedded with sensors and software that connect and exchange data over the internet.
Augmented reality overlays digital information, such as images or data, onto a person's real-world view, typically through a smartphone camera or headset.
Open-source software is released with a license granting users the right to view, modify, and distribute the source code, encouraging collaborative development.
The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 symbolized the end of the Cold War division between East and West Germany and paved the way for German reunification.
The Renaissance was a period of renewed interest in art, science, and classical learning that began in Italy in the 14th century and spread across Europe.
Ancient Mesopotamia, located between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, is often called the cradle of civilization due to its early developments in writing, agriculture, and urban life.
Chocolate is made from the fermented, roasted, and ground seeds of the cacao tree, a process refined over centuries into the sweet treat known today.
Paella is a Spanish rice dish originating from Valencia, traditionally cooked in a wide, shallow pan and often flavored with saffron, seafood, or meat.
Coffee beans are the seeds of berries from the Coffea plant, and their flavor is heavily influenced by growing region, roast level, and brewing method.
